stories.title: “It’s not an inquiry, it’s a review”: Welsh Government Covid panel can’t force ex-ministers to appear
stories.summary: The Welsh Government’s new review of the Covid pandemic in Wales will have no legal power to force former ministers or officials to give evidence. Dafydd Trystan Davies, Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution, announced the review-and-assurance panel for COVID-19 Wales in the Senedd on Tuesday. stories.title: Flintshire council can’t say if recycling centre cuts saved £250,000
stories.summary: Flintshire Council cannot say whether cutting recycling centre opening hours saved the £250,000 it was supposed to, according to an internal audit. The audit gives the council’s management of household recycling centres and fly-tipping the lowest rating of “limited assurance”. It will go before the council’s environment and economy scrutiny committee on Tuesday (10 November).

stories.title: Flintshire council missed 12,171 bins in nine months
stories.summary: Missed bin collections in Flintshire rose sharply in May and June, a report to councillors shows. It puts this down to driver shortages, reduced supervision and changes to collection rounds. Outstanding missed collection cases peaked at 1,582 in June 2026. stories.title: Greenfield Valley parkrun to welcome walkers for World Diabetes Day
stories.summary: Walkers are being invited to Greenfield Valley parkrun on Saturday 14 November to mark World Diabetes Day. The Greenfield Valley event is one of eight parkruns in Wales taking part in Parkwalk for Change, run by Diabetes UK Cymru with Public Health Wales and health boards.
